skill.name: allaymc-plugin-dev
skill.description: Create, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins in Java or other JVM languages using official templates, Gradle metadata, lifecycle guidance, and local reference sources.
skill.summary: Build and maintain AllayMC plugins with template setup, Gradle configuration, lifecycle implementation, and reference-guided troubleshooting.
skill.author: AllayMC

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans in setup and development guidance, plus ordinary LGPL license text. The only confirmed issues are expected Gradle run and build commands, which are legitimate but should remain user-approved because Gradle execution can run local build logic.

remediation.issue: Gradle wrapper commands may execute project-controlled build scripts during testing or packaging.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users before running ./gradlew runServer or ./gradlew shadowJar, and recommend reviewing build files in untrusted projects first.

remediation.issue: Many inline code spans describe file paths and identifiers, which can trigger automated command detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly separated from path and identifier references, and label commands as optional user-approved actions.

content.value_statement: AllayMC plugin setup requires correct templates, Gradle metadata, lifecycle classes, and API references. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through plugin creation, migration, testing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides new AllayMC plugin creation from the official JavaPluginTemplate.
Collects plugin name, package, author, website, and API version before setup.
Updates Gradle metadata, Java toolchain settings, and AllayGradle configuration.
Explains plugin entry class creation with AllayMC lifecycle methods.
Directs agents to local AllayMC, AllayGradle, and template references when needed.
Recommends local Gradle testing and shaded jar builds for configured projects.
limitations: It is focused on AllayMC plugin projects, not general Minecraft server administration.
It depends on bundled reference submodules being available and current.
It does not replace manual review of Gradle build scripts from untrusted projects.
It gives workflow guidance but does not guarantee runtime compatibility with every AllayMC version.

use_cases.title: Create a new plugin skeleton
use_cases.description: Generate an AllayMC plugin project from the official template with correct package, metadata, and entry class guidance.
use_cases.target_user: Java developers starting a new AllayMC plugin

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing JVM plugin
use_cases.description: Adapt Gradle metadata, package names, plugin descriptors, and lifecycle methods for an AllayMC target.
use_cases.target_user: Plugin authors moving code from another Minecraft server platform

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot plugin build issues
use_cases.description: Use local AllayMC and AllayGradle references to investigate API usage, build configuration, and lifecycle behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic plugin
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup from the official template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to create a new AllayMC plugin named MyFirstPlugin with package com.example.myfirstplugin.

prompt_templates.title: Configure project metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate Gradle and plugin metadata update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to update my existing AllayMC plugin metadata, Gradle group, version, authors, website, and API version.

prompt_templates.title: Add lifecycle behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to add onLoad, onEnable, and onDisable behavior to my AllayMC plugin entry class.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a build or API issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to inspect my plugin build failure, check the AllayGradle setup, and compare the API usage with local references.

output_examples.input: Create a new AllayMC plugin skeleton for a chat moderation plugin.
output: A short list of required project details to confirm before setup.
A project initialization plan based on the official Java template.
Guidance for package renaming, Gradle metadata, and entry class creation.

output_examples.input: Help me troubleshoot why my AllayMC plugin does not start.
output: A focused checklist covering plugin metadata, entry class configuration, lifecycle methods, and build output.
Pointers to relevant local AllayMC or AllayGradle references for deeper verification.

output_examples.input: Prepare my plugin for a local test run.
output: A review of configuration items that should be checked before running the server.
A reminder that local Gradle commands should be approved before execution.

best_practices: Confirm plugin name, package, author, website, and target API version before editing project files.
Review build files before running Gradle commands in projects from untrusted sources.
Use local AllayMC and AllayGradle references when API behavior is unclear.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a project uses JavaPluginTemplate without checking package and build structure.
Do not run Gradle wrapper commands without user approval in an untrusted workspace.
Do not overwrite defensive null or concurrency checks when updating plugin logic.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps create, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins written in Java or other JVM languages.

faq.question: Does it include AllayMC reference material?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill points agents to local AllayMC, AllayGradle, and JavaPluginTemplate references when available.

faq.question: Can it migrate an existing plugin?
faq.answer: It can guide metadata, package, descriptor, and lifecycle updates for an existing plugin project.

faq.question: Does it run the plugin automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends Gradle test and build commands, but users should approve command execution first.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm the reference submodules are present and review build scripts before running commands in untrusted projects.
